headline: Sales hold steady but separation costs drive a loss
summary_short: International Paper reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $6.00B (+0.6% q/q, -2.2% y/y) and swung to a net loss of $12M, or -$0.02 diluted EPS, from +$0.14 y/y.
summary_long: Net sales were $6.00B (+0.6% q/q, -2.2% y/y). PS North America sales rose to $3,688M on higher prices, volumes and mix, but segment profit fell to $204M on Riverdale conversion costs and higher maintenance outages. PS EMEA sales fell to $2,287M on soft demand, widening its operating loss to $80M. Diluted EPS swung to -$0.02 from $0.14 y/y on $54M of net special items, mainly $43M of PS EMEA separation costs. Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) fell to $587M (-13.3% q/q, -12.4% y/y); cash fell to $726M on debt paydown and dividends. IP guided Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $780-830M, including an $85M hit from the temporary Pine Hill, Alabama mill closure, and full-year Adjusted EBITDA of $3.20-3.40B.

drivers.explanation: PS North America sales rose on higher prices, volumes and favorable mix; PS EMEA sales fell as soft demand amid geopolitical uncertainty offset higher paper prices.
Swing to a loss reflects $54M of net special items, mainly $43M of PS EMEA separation costs, plus Riverdale conversion spend and higher planned-maintenance outages in North America.
EBITDA fell as PS EMEA's operating loss widened on lower volumes and unrealized paper-price gains, while North America absorbed higher maintenance-outage and conversion costs.
Management cites improving execution and accelerated EMEA cost-out ahead of the planned NA/EMEA separation, while flagging an $85M Pine Hill, Alabama mill-closure hit to Q3 EBITDA.
